t: Brueys anchored his 13 ships of the line in a line inside the bay, but left room between the leading ship and the shoal, and Nelson's ships passed through it and caught the French vanguard in a crossfire.
Of 17 French ships engaged, two ships of the line and two frigates escaped; the French flagship Orient blew up at about 22:00 with more than 1,000 men killed.
The defeat left Napoleon's army trapped in Egypt and gave the Royal Navy the dominant position in the Mediterranean that it kept for the rest of the Napoleonic Wars.
dyk: Nelson pursued the French for more than two months and passed their invasion convoy in the dark on 22 June, missing it by less than a day when he reached Alexandria on 28 June.
ev: Bonaparte's armada sails from Toulon for Egypt
Nelson's fleet passes the French convoy in the darkness without knowing it
Bonaparte lands in Egypt and takes Alexandria, and Brueys anchors in Aboukir Bay
The British fleet attacks the French at about 18:20 on the 1st and the French flagship Orient explodes at 22:00
Fighting resumes on the 2nd and the last French ship of the line destroyed or captured, Timoléon, blows up on the 3rd
News of the victory reaches Britain and Nelson is made Baron Nelson of the Nile

f.date: 1 to 3 August 1798; the main fighting began at about 18:20 on 1 August
f.place: Aboukir Bay, on the Mediterranean coast of Egypt, about 20 miles (32 km) north-east of Alexandria
f.sides: The Royal Navy under Rear-Admiral Sir Horatio Nelson, with 13 ships of the line, and the French Navy under Vice-admiral François-Paul Brueys d'Aigalliers, with 13 ships of the line and four frigates; 17 French ships were engaged
f.outcome: Brueys was killed and his flagship Orient blew up; only two French ships of the line and two frigates escaped, and Napoleon's army was left in Egypt without a fleet.
